source.citation: Honorio, T., Bary, B., Sanahuja, J., Benboudjema, F. (2017). Effective properties of n-coated composite spheres assemblage in an ageing linear viscoelastic framework. International Journal of Solids and Structures 124, 1-13.
source.location: Table 1, p. 7; equations (46) and (47), p. 6; section 5

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), read on the page text and compared with the image of the page
transcription.note: Parameters of the generalized Maxwell models of the two aging phases: the bulk and shear relaxation functions are k(t,t') = (k0 + sum_j kj exp(-(t-t')/tau_j)) f_age(t') and the same with mu, with the aging function f_age(t') = 3/4 (1 - exp(-t')), t' in days (equations (46) and (47)). Phase 1, the core, is elastic. Phase 0 is the matrix and phase 2 the coating. Moduli in GPa, times in days.

E_core.description: Young modulus of the elastic core.

nu_core.description: Poisson ratio of the elastic core.

aging_amplitude.description: Factor of the aging function f_age(t') = 3/4 (1 - exp(-t'/1 day)).

inclusion_fraction.description: Volume fraction of the inclusions; in the three-phase case, 0.25 of core and 0.15 of coating.

notes: Table 1 also lists a Young modulus and a Poisson ratio for the two aging phases (30 GPa and 0.2, 40 GPa and 0.2), which the relaxation functions of equations (46) and (47) do not use.
